name: @restregular/dsh-visual-browser
description: Visual browser for DeepSeek Harness: a right-sidebar tab under the built-in Browser that streams Chrome live as a binary JPEG frame stream (no screenshot polling) while the Agent drives it through a token-light numbered view of interactive elements, never the raw DOM, and hands each acting tool back the picture itself so click → screenshot → read is one call. The panel keeps real pages as Chrome-style tabs that always show, adopts tabs the page opens itself, reorders by drag with a frosted-glass lift, carries a right-click menu (refresh, copy the link, open it in your own default browser, reference the page in the chat, close, close all), suggests the browsing history under the address box in every tab (title - domain rows, prefix filtering, arrow-key picking, per-entry delete), can be handed over to the Agent with a Follow switch that locks it behind an orange-edged mask while the live picture jumps to whichever tab the Agent touches, forwards clicks, drags, wheel and typing straight to the DevTools input domain, fills native file choosers with real paths and writes the values of native date / time / colour pickers that no picture can show, draws its own cursor scaled to the picture, locks the view with a tinted veil while the Agent acts, draws its clicks, scrolls and drags, and shows the active page's own console where scripts can be run. Starts Chrome as an ordinary browser — no webdriver flag, no HeadlessChrome User-Agent, a desktop-sized screen — so sites that bind a login to the browser they hand it to (doubao.com and other ByteDance properties) keep the session instead of signing it out.
author: RestRegular
